name: Event-Driven Architecture
description: Enforce event-driven communication patterns, schema governance, and channel hygiene

rules.name: Async Communication Via Event Channels
rules.description: All asynchronous communication between services must go through documented event channels. Direct async calls without a channel create invisible coupling and make the system harder to observe.

config.message: Asynchronous relationship must be routed through a documented event channel.

rules.name: Event Schema Required
rules.description: Every event channel must have a defined schema contract (AsyncAPI, Avro, Protobuf, or JSON Schema). Untyped events cause silent failures and make consumer development guesswork.

config.message: Event channel must have an associated schema contract (AsyncAPI, Avro, Protobuf, or JSON Schema).

rules.name: No Direct Calls For Async Operations
rules.description: Operations that are inherently asynchronous (notifications, background processing, data sync) must not use synchronous service-to-service calls. Use event channels to decouple producers from consumers.

config.message: Async operations must use event channels, not synchronous service-to-service calls.

rules.name: Event Channel Must Have Producer and Consumer
rules.description: Every event channel must have at least one producer and one consumer linked to it. Orphaned channels are dead code in the architecture and indicate missing or broken integrations.

config.message: Event channel must have at least one producer and one consumer. Remove orphaned channels or complete the integration.

rules.name: Dead Letter Queue Required
rules.description: All event consumers must have an associated dead letter queue (DLQ) for handling failed messages. Without a DLQ, poison messages can block processing or be silently lost.

config.message: Event channel consumers must have an associated dead letter queue for failed message handling.

rules.name: Event Naming Convention
rules.description: Event channel names must follow the domain.action format (e.g., order.created, payment.completed) for consistent discoverability and clear semantics.

config.message: Event channel name must follow domain.action format (e.g., order.created, user.registered).

rules.name: Event Channel Description Required
rules.description: Every event channel must have a description explaining its purpose, expected payload shape, and typical consumers. This is essential for team discoverability in event-driven systems.

config.message: Event channel must have a description explaining its purpose and expected usage.

rules.name: No Bidirectional Event Channels
rules.description: A single event channel must not be used for both request and response between the same two services. This creates hidden coupling. Use separate channels for commands and replies.

config.message: Event channel must not be used bidirectionally between the same services. Use separate channels for request and response.
